1	# Evaluate — Design and run Flow evaluations
2	
3	Capability index for `uip maestro flow eval` — evaluator CRUD (7 types), eval set CRUD with entry-point pinning, data point management with file attachments, and Studio Web run start/status/results/list/compare. Local CRUD is offline; runs require `uip login` and a Flow solution that already exists in Studio Web.
4	
5	> **Where you came from / where to go next.** Evaluate is downstream of Operate (ship the flow → evaluate it on Studio Web) and feeds back into Author (failing eval → fix the `.flow` → re-ship → re-evaluate). Build/edit lives in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md); publish/deploy lives in [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../operate/CAPABILITY.md); fault triage on a debug or process run lives in [diagnose/CAPABILITY.md](../diagnose/CAPABILITY.md).
6	>
7	> **Inherits universal rules from [SKILL.md](../../SKILL.md)** — `--output json` + prefer `--output-filter` for extraction, no `flow debug` without consent, never invoke other skills automatically, dropdown question pattern, **plain-English narration + granular progress list (opt-in — silent by default; engage when the user asks for verbosity)**. The rules below are evaluate-scoped and apply on top.
8	
9	## When to use this capability
10	
11	- Add or remove data points (test cases) on a Flow eval set
12	- Create evaluators (`exact-match`, `json-similarity`, `contains`, `llm-judge-*` types) for a Flow project
13	- Create or remove eval sets, link them to evaluators, pin entry points
14	- Add, list, or remove simulations on data points (`uip maestro flow eval simulation`)
15	- Start an eval run on Studio Web, poll its status, fetch detailed results
16	- Compare two eval runs to verify a change improved scores without regressions
17	
18	For agent (`agent.json`) evaluations read the `uipath-agents` skill. For BPMN evaluations read the `uipath-maestro-bpmn` skill — this capability covers Flow only.
19	
20	## Critical rules
21	
22	1. **Check Flow eval CLI availability once.** Run `uip maestro flow eval --help --output json` before using eval commands. If it returns `unknown command 'eval'`, the installed CLI does not expose Flow eval yet. Stop, report that the user needs a CLI/tool version with Flow eval support, and do not spend turns searching npm packages or source bundles.
23	<!--skill-flavor:upload-safety-critical-rule:start-->
24	2. **Never run `uip solution upload` automatically as part of an eval workflow.** The eval run requires the Flow solution to already exist in Studio Web, but uploading from the local working tree clobbers whatever is on Studio Web. If the project was pulled from Studio Web (`uip solution download`), edited locally in VS Code, or scaffolded on disk and never uploaded, an unprompted upload will overwrite or push unintended state. Ask the user explicitly before any `uip solution upload` — see [upload-safety.md](references/upload-safety.md).
25	<!--skill-flavor:upload-safety-critical-rule:end-->
26	3. **`--path` accepts a Flow project directory OR a solution directory containing exactly one Flow project.** If the solution holds multiple Flow projects, point `--path` at the specific project directory.
27	4. **Local CRUD does not require login.** `add`, `remove`, `list` (data points / eval sets / evaluators) edit JSON on disk. Only `uip maestro flow eval run *` requires `uip login` and an existing Studio Web solution.
28	5. **Pin a model on every LLM-judge evaluator.** Empty/missing `model` produces a cryptic 500 from the LLM gateway after retries. Pass `--model <name>` on `evaluator add` or set `model` in the JSON.
29	6. **Declare input variables before adding data points with `--inputs`.** `eval add` validates input keys against the Flow's declared input variables and fails fast on unknown keys. Add missing input variables first (for example, `uip maestro flow variable add My.flow name --direction in --type string --output json`) or change the data point input JSON to match the Flow schema.
30	7. **Let the CLI manage evaluator references.** Eval sets store `evaluatorRefs` as the evaluator file refs produced by `evaluator add` (for example, `greeting-match-1234abcd.json`). If the set should use every evaluator that already exists, omit `--evaluators` so the CLI writes those generated file refs. If you must pass `--evaluators`, pass the evaluator id or generated file base/ref from `evaluator add/list` — never the display name alone (`greeting-match`), because Studio Web does not resolve display-name refs.
31	8. **Pre-empt timeouts on `run start --wait`.** The CLI blocks until the run reaches a terminal state or `--timeout` elapses. `--timeout` only stops local blocking — the run continues server-side; query progress with `eval run status <run_id>`.
32	
33	## Quick Start
34	
35	Standard workflow: scaffold evaluators → create eval set → add data points → confirm project is in Studio Web → run.
36	
37	```bash
38	# 1. Add an evaluator (local; no login required)
39	uip maestro flow eval evaluator add greeting-quality \
40	  --type llm-judge-output \
41	  --model gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 \
42	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
43	
44	# 2. Create an eval set, pin the entry point, and let the CLI attach
45	#    all current evaluators by generated file ref
46	uip maestro flow eval set add "Smoke Tests" \
47	  --entry-point /Main.bpmn#start \
48	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
49	
50	# 3. Add data points (test cases)
51	#    The `message` key must already be declared as a Flow input variable.
52	uip maestro flow eval add hello-test \
53	  --set "Smoke Tests" \
54	  --inputs '{"message":"hello"}' \
55	  --expected '{"reply":"Hello! How can I help you?"}' \
56	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
57	
58	<!--skill-flavor:upload-safety-workflow-comment:start-->
59	# 4. Confirm the solution is in Studio Web
60	#    DO NOT auto-run `uip solution upload`. Ask the user. See upload-safety.md.
61	<!--skill-flavor:upload-safety-workflow-comment:end-->
62	
63	# 5. Start the run and wait
64	uip maestro flow eval run start \
65	  --set "Smoke Tests" \
66	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow \
67	  --wait --timeout 600 --output json
68	
69	# 6. Inspect failures
70	uip maestro flow eval run results <eval_set_run_id> \
71	  --set "Smoke Tests" \
72	  --only-failed --verbose \
73	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
74	```

1	# `uip maestro flow eval` Command Reference
2	
3	Complete syntax reference for every subcommand under `uip maestro flow eval`. All commands accept the global flags `--output <table|json|yaml|plain>` (default `json`), `--output-filter <jmespath>`, `--log-level <debug|info|warn|error>`, and `--log-file <path>`. Repeated reminders below: always pass `--output json` when an agent will parse the result.
4	
5	## Command Tree
6	
7	```
8	uip maestro flow eval
9	├── add        — Add a data point to an evaluation set
10	├── list       — List data points in an evaluation set
11	├── remove     — Remove a data point from an evaluation set
12	├── set
13	│   ├── add    — Create an evaluation set
14	│   ├── list   — List evaluation sets
15	│   └── remove — Remove an evaluation set
16	├── evaluator
17	│   ├── add    — Add an evaluator to the flow project
18	│   ├── list   — List evaluators in a flow project
19	│   └── remove — Remove an evaluator from a flow project
20	├── simulation
21	│   ├── add    — Add or update a simulation on a data point
22	│   ├── list   — List simulations on a data point
23	│   └── remove — Remove a simulation from a data point
24	└── run
25	    ├── start    — Start a Studio Web evaluation run
26	    ├── status   — Check the status of a run
27	    ├── results  — Get detailed per-data-point results
28	    ├── list     — List runs for an eval set
29	    └── compare  — Compare two runs side-by-side
30	```
31	
32	`add` / `remove` / `list` at the top level operate on **data points** (test cases) inside an eval set. Data points are stored inline within the eval set JSON, not as separate files.
33	
34	## Common Options
35	
36	Every subcommand accepts:
37	
38	| Flag | Required | Description |
39	|------|----------|-------------|
40	| `--path <path>` | No (defaults to `.`) | Flow project directory, or a solution directory containing exactly one Flow project |
41	| `--output <fmt>` | No (default `json`) | `table`, `json`, `yaml`, or `plain` |
42	| `--output-filter <expr>` | No | JMESPath expression applied to JSON output before printing |
43	
44	## Data Points (Test Cases)
45	
46	### `uip maestro flow eval add <name>`
47	
48	Add a data point to an eval set.
49	
50	| Flag | Required | Description |
51	|------|----------|-------------|
52	| `--set <name>` | Yes | Eval set name or ID |
53	| `--inputs <json>` | No | Input values as a JSON object; keys must be declared as Flow input variables |
54	| `--input-file <key=path>` | No | Attach a file as input `<key>`; **repeatable** |
55	| `--expected <json>` | No | Expected output as a JSON object |
56	| `--criteria <json>` | No | Per-evaluator criteria JSON object keyed by evaluator id |
57	| `--search-text <text>` | No | Search text for `contains` evaluators |
58	| `--path <path>` | No | (see Common Options) |
59	
60	Example:
61	
62	```bash
63	uip maestro flow eval add greeting-test \
64	  --set "Smoke Tests" \
65	  --inputs '{"name":"Alice"}' \
66	  --expected '{"greeting":"Hello, Alice!"}' \
67	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
68	```
69	
70	### `uip maestro flow eval list`
71	
72	List data points in an eval set.
73	
74	```bash
75	uip maestro flow eval list --set "Smoke Tests" --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json
76	```
77	
78	### `uip maestro flow eval remove <id>`
79	
80	Remove a data point. `<id>` accepts the data point's UUID or its `name`.
81	
82	## Evaluation Sets
83	
84	### `uip maestro flow eval set add <name>`
85	
86	Create an evaluation set.
87	
88	| Flag | Required | Description |
89	|------|----------|-------------|
90	| `--evaluators <refs>` | No (default: all) | Comma-separated evaluator IDs or generated file base names; do not pass display names |
91	| `--entry-point <id>` | No | Entry point node id stored as the eval set's `selectedEntrypoint` |
92	| `--path <path>` | No | (see Common Options) |
93	
94	When `--evaluators` is omitted, the new eval set references **all** evaluators present in the project at creation time using their generated evaluator file refs. Prefer this when creating a set immediately after adding the evaluator(s). If passing `--evaluators`, use the generated id/file base returned by `evaluator add/list`, not the evaluator display name.
95	
96	### `uip maestro flow eval set list`
97	
98	List eval sets in the project.
99	
100	### `uip maestro flow eval set remove <id>`
101	
102	Remove an eval set. `<id>` accepts the eval set's UUID, `name`, or file base name.
103	
104	## Evaluators
105	
106	### `uip maestro flow eval evaluator add <name>`
107	
108	Create an evaluator file in the project's evaluators directory.
109	
110	| Flag | Required | Description |
111	|------|----------|-------------|
112	| `--type <type>` | Yes | One of: `exact-match`, `json-similarity`, `contains`, `llm-judge-output`, `llm-judge-strict-json`, `llm-judge-trajectory`, `llm-judge-trajectory-simulation` |
113	| `--description <text>` | No | Evaluator description |
114	| `--target-key <key>` | No | Output key the evaluator scores against (defaults to `*` — the entire output) |

131	## Simulations
132	
133	Simulations intercept specific nodes (connectors, agents, sub-flows) during an eval run and replace their real execution with a controlled response. Each simulation targets a single component by its `componentId` and applies one of three strategies.
134	
135	### `uip maestro flow eval simulation add <component-id>`
136	
137	Add or replace a simulation on a data point. If a simulation for `<component-id>` already exists on the data point it is overwritten.
138	
139	| Flag | Required | Description |
140	|------|----------|-------------|
141	| `--set <name>` | Yes | Eval set name or ID |
142	| `--data-point <id>` | Yes | Data point name or ID |
143	| `--strategy <strategy>` | Yes | `Llm` or `Static` |
144	| `--component-type <type>` | Yes | Component type (e.g. `connector`, `agent`, `subflow`) |
145	| `--component-description <text>` | No | Human-readable label for the component |
146	| `--simulation-instructions <text>` | No | LLM prompt describing what the component should return (for `Llm` strategy) |
147	| `--mock-value <json>` | No | Static JSON output (for `Static` strategy) |
148	| `--output-schema <json>` | No | JSON Schema describing the expected output shape; passed to the LLM to constrain its response. **Auto-resolved from the `.flow` file when omitted for `Llm` strategy** — fails if the node is not found or has no outputs. Pass explicitly to override. |
149	| `--path <path>` | No | (see Common Options) |
150	
151	**Strategy guide:**
152	
153	| Strategy | When to use | Key flags |
154	|----------|-------------|-----------|
155	| `Llm` | Output should be realistic but non-deterministic | `--simulation-instructions`, `--output-schema` (auto-resolved) |
156	| `Static` | Output is fixed and deterministic | `--mock-value` |
157	
158	**`--output-schema` auto-resolution for Llm simulations:** When omitted, the CLI reads the `.flow` file, finds the node by `<component-id>`, and derives the schema from the node's output definition (connector `outputJsonSchema`, agent `agentOutputVariables`, or `node.outputs`). Fails with an actionable error if the node is not found or has no outputs. Pass `--output-schema` explicitly to override. The JSON Schema is sent alongside `--simulation-instructions` to the LLM, telling it what shape the output must conform to. Without it the LLM generates free-form text. For a connector that returns `{ status, message }` you would pass:
159	
160	```bash
161	--output-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"status":{"type":"string"},"message":{"type":"string"}}}'
162	```

168	  --set "Smoke Tests" \
169	  --data-point "hello-test" \
170	  --strategy Llm \
171	  --component-type connector \
172	  --simulation-instructions "Pretend to send the email and return a success confirmation." \
173	  --path ./MySolution/MyFlow --output json

7	## Should you plan first?
8	
9	For complex flows, produce a plan before building. Reference [planning-arch.md](planning-arch.md) and [planning-impl.md](planning-impl.md) for the node type catalog, port reference, wiring rules, and topology patterns.
10	
11	**Plan when:**
12	- The flow has 5+ nodes with branching or parallel paths
13	- The flow uses connectors or resources that need discovery
14	- The user's requirements are ambiguous and you need to confirm the approach
15	
16	**Don't plan when:**
17	- Adding/editing a single node in an existing flow (use [brownfield.md](brownfield.md))
18	- The flow is a straightforward linear pipeline (trigger → action → action → end)
19	- The user has already described the exact topology they want

22	
23	**Plan:** "Build a flow that receives a Jira ticket, classifies it with an AI agent, routes urgent tickets to Slack and non-urgent to a queue, and logs everything to a Google Sheet."

33	## Three-turn execution map
34	
35	Steps 0–6 are **logical phases**, not separate turns. A typical greenfield build collapses to **three assistant turns** (universal SKILL.md rule #10). Each step heading below carries a `[T1]` / `[T2]` / `[T3]` tag — emit every tool call inside the same Turn as one assistant message.
36	
37	| Turn | Steps | What you emit in ONE assistant message |
38	|---|---|---|
39	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-execution-map-intro:end-->
40	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:start-->
41	| **T1 — Setup + discovery** | 0, 1, 2, 3 | One chained `Bash` (scaffold + register + pull + `node add` for each CLI-owned node) **+** parallel `Bash` (one `registry get` per OOTB type you'll inline) **+** parallel `Read` (plugin `impl.md`s). **If existing `.uipx` solutions are present, the Step 2 gate fires first in its own turn** — resolve it before this chain. |
42	| **T2 — Read + author** | 4 | One `Read` of the `.flow` **+** a batch of `Edit` calls (or one `Write` if ≥70% of nodes change). Claude Code serializes Edits on the same file, so they don't race |
43	| **T3 — Finalize** | 5, 6 | One chained `Bash` (`node configure && validate && format`). On validate failure: one Edit turn, then re-chain `validate && format` |
44	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:end-->
45	
46	### Batching anti-patterns
47	
48	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:start-->
49	- **One CLI per turn.** Never issue `solution init`, then `cd`, then `flow init` as three separate Bash calls — chain with `&&`, the `cd` included as its own segment. Same for `node configure && validate && format`.
50	- **Sequential `registry get`s.** Emit every `registry get` as a parallel `Bash` in one message alongside the T1 scaffold chain.
51	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:end-->
52	- **Validating after every Edit.** Validate once at the end of T3 (or after a recovery Edit). Intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
53	- **Re-reading the `.flow` every turn.** `Read` once at the start of T2; subsequent `Edit`s in the same conversation don't need re-reading unless an external command (e.g., `node configure`, `format`) rewrites the file between Edits.
54	- **`Edit` in the same turn as a `Bash` that mutates the same file.** Parallel tool calls race — separate them across turns.
55	- **Two parallel `Edit`s anchored to the same byte range.** Same-file Edits serialize in execution order; if Edit N's `old_string` overlaps text that Edit N-1's substitution removed or shifted, Edit N fails with "string not found." Use the [per-array anchor pattern](#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order) — anchor each Edit on its target array's own opening key, never on key order or a shared boundary.

85	## Step 2 — Create a solution, THEN a Flow project inside it **[T1]**
86	
87	> **A Flow project cannot exist outside a solution** (universal rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). Run `uip maestro flow init` (Step 2b) outside a solution and it now **auto-scaffolds** one — `<Project>Solution/<Project>Solution.uipx` with the project nested at `<Project>Solution/<Project>/` (response carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution`). Still scaffold or select the solution first (Step 2a) so you set the solution name yourself rather than the auto `<Project>Solution`, and so discovery is unambiguous. The solution and project names are independent — they need not match. The correct layout is **always** `<Solution>/<Project>/<Project>.flow` (double-nested — see the tree after Step 2c). Passing `--skip-solution-registration` opts out of both auto-scaffold and registration, leaving a bare single-nested layout that fails Studio Web upload and packaging.
88	
89	Check for existing solutions with `find . -maxdepth 2 -type f -name '*.uipx' -print` (each solution is its own folder — `<Solution>/<Solution>.uipx` — so a bare `*.uipx` glob misses them). If any are found, **STOP before the T1 chain — do not run `uip solution init` yet** — and ask the user which solution to use per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md) (rules #5 and #6): one option per discovered `.uipx`, a **"Create a new solution"** option, and **"Something else"** last. Rule #5 owns the ask mechanism (structured `AskUserQuestion` where the runtime offers it, a numbered chat list otherwise, recommended-option fallback when non-interactive) — do not re-specify a tool here. Applies even when the user wants a new solution. If none are found, create a new one automatically.

91	- If the user specifies an existing `.uipx` file path or solution name, use that (skip to Step 2b)

94	### Canonical T1 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
95	
96	This is the consolidated command that does Steps 2a + 2b + Step 3 + (optionally) one `node add` per CLI-owned node, in one chained Bash. `node add` signature is `<file> <node-type>` (file first):
97	
98	```bash
99	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json \
100	  && cd "<SolutionName>" \
101	  && uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>" --output json \
102	  && cd "<ProjectName>" \
103	  && uip maestro flow registry pull \
104	  && uip maestro flow node add "<ProjectName>.flow" core.action.http.v2 --label "<NodeLabel>" --output json
105	```
106	
107	> **One creation path — never drop the `cd`.** `uip solution init "<SolutionName>"` → `cd "<SolutionName>"` → `uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>"`, one chain. Without the `cd`, `flow init` runs in the old directory and auto-scaffolds a duplicate `<ProjectName>Solution/` (1-node husk). Never let auto-scaffold create the solution. Finish with exactly one `project.uiproj` — delete strays.
108	
109	Tail-append one `node add` per CLI-owned node (`uipath.connector.*`, `uipath.connector.trigger.*`, `core.action.http.v2`). Each `node add` returns the new node `id` in `Data` — capture it from the chained output for T2/T3. Drop the trailing `node add` segment when the flow is OOTB-only.
110	
111	In the SAME assistant message (parallel to this chain): emit one `Bash` per OOTB `registry get <NODE_TYPE>` you'll need in T2 (always `core.control.end` — see Step 4), and parallel `Read` calls for any plugin `impl.md`s you'll consult.
112	
113	> **Older `solution-tool` (< 1.0.0)** used `solution new` (see [.claude/rules/cli-renames.md](../../../../../.claude/rules/cli-renames.md)). If `solution init` returns `unknown command`, substitute `solution new`.

115	The sub-steps below describe what each command in the chain does and how to verify the result.
116	
117	### 2a. Create a new solution
118	
119	```bash
120	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json
121	```
122	
123	Creates `<cwd>/<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx`. **`cd` into the new solution directory before Step 2b.**
124	
125	> **Naming convention:** In **pure greenfield** (no existing solutions), default the solution name to the project name unless the user specifies otherwise. When solutions already exist and the user chooses "Create a new solution", **ask for the new solution's name** — do not reuse the project name (SKILL.md rule #6). The two names are independent.
126	
127	### 2b. Create the Flow project inside the solution folder
128	
129	```bash
130	cd <directory>/<SolutionName> && uip maestro flow init <ProjectName> --output json
131	```
132	
133	The `cd` puts the project inside the solution you just created. Skip it and `flow init` won't find that solution (discovery walks **up**, not down into `<SolutionName>/`) — it auto-scaffolds a **second, separate** `<ProjectName>Solution/` beside your empty `<SolutionName>/`, leaving two solutions. The project no longer single-nests, but `cd` first to land in the right one.
134	
135	> **Bash session state persists across tool calls.** This `cd` is **not scoped to one Bash invocation** — your cwd remains inside `<SolutionName>/` for every subsequent `Bash` call until you `cd` somewhere else. Plan the rest of Step 2 (and Steps 3–6) accordingly: either keep using paths relative to the solution dir, or anchor with `$(pwd)` / the absolute `Data.Path` returned by `flow init`. Do NOT prefix later commands with the original `<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` — that would resolve as `<SolutionName>/<directory>/<SolutionName>/...` and look like a layout bug when it isn't.
136	
137	`--output json` is required so Step 2c can inspect `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` to confirm the project was auto-registered with the parent solution.

139	### 2c. Verify the project is registered in the solution
140	
141	When `uip maestro flow init` is run from inside a solution directory (Step 2b), it **auto-registers** the project with the nearest parent `.uipx`. Run outside any solution, it **auto-scaffolds** `<Project>Solution/` and registers the project in it — the response then also carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution` (`{ Name, Path, SolutionFile }`) and `Status: Registered`. Pass `--skip-solution-registration` to opt out of both (Status `OptedOut`, bare single-nested layout). The success envelope always reports the outcome in `Data.SolutionRegistration`:
142	
143	```json
144	{
145	  "Result": "Success",
146	  "Code": "FlowInit",
147	  "Data": {
148	    "Status": "Created successfully",
149	    "Path": ".../<SolutionName>/<ProjectName>",
150	    "SolutionRegistration": {
151	      "Status": "Registered",                     // or "AlreadyRegistered"
152	      "Solution": ".../<SolutionName>.uipx",
153	      "Project": "<ProjectName>/project.uiproj",
154	      "ProjectId": "<uuid>"
155	    }
156	  }
157	}
158	```
159	
160	If `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` is `Registered` or `AlreadyRegistered`, **you are done** with this step — proceed to the layout check. If it is `OptedOut`, you passed `--skip-solution-registration` and the skip was intentional.
161	
162	**Fallback** — when `Status` is `Skipped` (ambiguous discovery — e.g. multiple `.uipx`), `Failed` (the `.uipx` write failed), or `NotInSolution` (rare — auto-scaffold did not run and no parent `.uipx` was found): wire the project manually.

168	```

260	## Step 4 — Build the flow **[T2]**
261	
262	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-build-scaffold-assumptions:start-->
263	> **`flow init` scaffolds ONLY the manual trigger (`start` / `core.trigger.manual`) with zero edges.** Every other user-owned node — **including the End node** — is yours to add via `Edit` / `Write`. Any HTTP / connector / connector-trigger node you `node add`-ed in T1 is already in `nodes[]` and `definitions[]` but has empty `inputs.detail` (filled in T3) and is not wired yet.
264	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-build-scaffold-assumptions:end-->
265	
266	### T2 batch — issue these in ONE assistant message
267	
268	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:start-->
269	1. **One `Read`** of `<ProjectName>.flow` — required before any Edit/Write; T1's chained Bash mutated the file and Claude Code's file-state tracker does not auto-refresh on external mutations.
270	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:end-->
271	2. **A batch of parallel `Edit` calls** — one per top-level array you're modifying. Same-file Edits serialize in execution order, so each `old_string` must anchor to text NO OTHER parallel Edit modifies. Use the **per-array anchor pattern** below.
272	   - Edit `nodes[]` — add the End node (and any other user-owned nodes).
273	   - Edit `definitions[]` — paste the End definition verbatim from T1's `registry get core.control.end` output.
274	   - Edit `edges[]` — wire `trigger → <httpNode> → end`. End-node `outputs` mapping goes here too if you declared an `out` variable in `variables.globals`.
275	   - Edit `layout.nodes` — placeholder `{ position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, size: { width: 96, height: 96 }, collapsed: false }` per new node; `format` rewrites both position and size (by node shape) in T3.
276	
277	   `Write` of the whole file is allowed but token-costly on flows >~10 nodes — only fall back to `Write` when ≥70% of nodes change AND the file is small (see [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder)). **Never `Write` a flow that already has connector / connector-trigger / managed-HTTP nodes** — the rewrite clobbers their CLI-owned `bindings[]` / `inputs.detail` (invisible to `flow validate`); `Edit` in place, or re-run `node configure` as the last write. See [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node).
278	
279	#### Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits — anchor on what you Read, not on key order
280	
281	> **Do not assume a top-level key order.** The CLI does not guarantee which keys are present or in what sequence — fixtures show `runtime` before `nodes` on one flow and absent on another, and `bindings` / `variables` / `solutionId` / `projectId` / `metadata` appear in varying positions. Any anchor of the form "closing `]` + the NEXT top-level key" is coupled to that ordering and will silently break across CLI versions or between flows. **Anchor on the target array's OWN key instead — you just `Read` the file at the top of T2, so anchor to text that read actually contains.**
282	
283	Anchor each Edit using its target array's own opening key, located in the text you just Read — not adjacency to a neighbor key. The catch: `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique in the file. They recur **inside inline `definitions[]`** (an HTTP v2 / agent / subprocess definition embeds its own nested `nodes`/`edges`) **and inside any `subflows.<id>` block** (each subflow holds its own `nodes`/`edges`) — so even a small flow can carry several copies. The reliable, version-independent discriminator is **indentation: the top-level array sits at 2-space indent; every nested one is deeper.** `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` appear once each, so they need no disambiguation.
284	
285	| Edit target | Anchor on (from the text you Read) | How to insert |
286	|---|---|---|
287	| Append to `nodes[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "nodes": [` (the top-level array — deeper-indented `"nodes": ["` inside definitions do not match the two-leading-space prefix) plus the `start` node's opening `{ "id": "start"`. | Insert the new node object as the first element, immediately after the `[`: `\n    { new node JSON },`. Head-insertion keeps `old_string` clear of the array's closing `]`. |
288	| Append to `edges[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "edges": [`. A newly generated scaffold commonly has `\n  "edges": []`; the 2-space prefix distinguishes it from nested `edges` arrays. | When empty, replace `\n  "edges": []` with `\n  "edges": [\n    { new edge JSON }\n  ]`. When non-empty, anchor through the first edge and insert the new edge as the first element. |
289	| Append to `definitions[]` | `"definitions": [` plus the first definition's opening bytes. Top-level `definitions[]` is the only one in the file, so this is reliably unique. | Insert the new definition right after the opening `[`, as the first element. Never anchor on whatever key follows `definitions` — that key varies (`runtime`, `bindings`, `variables`, `layout`, depending on CLI version and what the flow contains). |
290	| Add an entry to `layout.nodes` | `"layout": {\n    "nodes": {\n      "start":` — `start` is the always-present trigger and the first key under `layout.nodes` in newly generated flows. The top-level `"layout": {` is the only one. | `"layout":` + `"start":` jointly disambiguate. Insert `"<newId>": { ... },\n      ` before `"start":`. CLI-owned nodes added via `node add` already have a `layout.nodes` entry — only add entries for nodes you author by hand (e.g. End). |
291	
292	**Why head-insertion.** Inserting the new element right after the array's opening `[` means the `old_string` never includes the array's closing `]` — so it cannot collide with a closing `]` from a nested object (`form.sections[].fields[]`), and it never references a sibling top-level key whose position is not guaranteed. JSON array element order is not semantically significant for `nodes` / `edges` / `definitions`, so head vs. tail insertion is equivalent; `flow format` normalizes layout regardless.
293	
294	**Disjointness rule.** Two parallel Edits MUST anchor on DIFFERENT top-level arrays — nodes-Edit on the top-level `nodes[]`, edges-Edit on the top-level `edges[]`, definitions-Edit on `definitions[]`, layout-Edit on `layout.nodes`. Because each anchors on its own array (not a shared boundary), the parallel Edits never overlap — provided each anchor is unique first (see below).
295	
296	**Pre-flight uniqueness check.** Before submitting an Edit, confirm your `old_string` appears **exactly once** in the file you Read. `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` are reliably unique. `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT — they recur inside inline definitions and subflows, so anchor on the **2-space-indented** occurrence and extend through the first element's opening (e.g. `"id": "start"`) until the match count is one. Never anchor on a bare bracket shape, and never assume the first textual occurrence is the top-level one.
297	
298	**Safer fallback when in doubt:** serialize the Edits across two turns. One extra turn is cheaper than a failed-Edit recovery loop (which forces a re-Read, a re-derived anchor, and a re-submit).
299	
300	See [shared/file-format.md — Top-level structure](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure) for which top-level keys exist and the note that their order is not guaranteed.
301	
302	> **Intra-turn ordering.** If a parallel `Edit` fails with "file not read," split `Read` into its own turn (cost: +1 turn).
303	
304	### Node ownership recap
305	
306	> **Before each node, classify it as user-owned or CLI-owned (see [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node)). Connector activities, connector triggers, and `core.action.http.v2` are CLI-only — use `uip maestro flow node add` + `uip maestro flow node configure`, never Edit. Hand-writing these will fail `flow validate`.**
307	
308	Edit `<ProjectName>.flow` directly in the project root. The `bindings_v2.json` file is also in the project root for resource bindings.
309	
310	> **Tool selection by ownership.** Use `Edit` for in-place changes to user-owned nodes; `Write` only when ≥70% of nodes change **and the flow has no CLI-owned nodes** (a full-file `Write` over connector / managed-HTTP nodes clobbers their `bindings[]` — see the Step 4 `Write` note above). For CLI-owned nodes (above), use `uip maestro flow node add` + `node configure` — see the relevant plugin's `impl.md` for the full configuration workflow. Inline-agent project scaffolding uses `uip agent init --inline-in-flow`, but inline-agent flow node/wiring edits are direct `.flow` JSON (the agent node itself is user-owned).
311	
312	Read [editing-operations.md](editing-operations.md) for strategy selection and per-operation recipes.
313	
314	> **Self-check before each mutation:** name the tool you're about to use. If the answer isn't `Edit`, `Write`, or `uip maestro flow ...` — STOP and ask the user (per the dropdown question rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). `python`, `node`, `jq`, `sed`, `awk`, and shell heredocs are a last resort and require explicit user approval after you've surfaced the trade-offs. See [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder).
315	
316	For each node type, follow the relevant plugin's `impl.md` for node-specific inputs, JSON structure, and configuration. The operations guides cover the mechanics (how to add/remove/wire); the plugins cover the semantics (what inputs and model fields each node type needs).
317	
318	## Step 5 — Validate **[T3 — chain with Step 6, plus any T1 `node configure`]**
319	
320	### Canonical T3 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
321	
322	```bash
323	uip maestro flow node configure "<ProjectName>.flow" "<httpNodeId>" --detail '<DETAIL_JSON>' --output json \
324	  && uip maestro flow validate "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json \
325	  && uip maestro flow format "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json
326	```
327	
328	`<DETAIL_JSON>` is node-type-specific — the schema is owned by each CLI-owned node's plugin, not duplicated here: HTTP → [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md#critical-use-node-configure), connectors → [connector/impl.md](plugins/connector/impl.md), connector triggers → [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md). Tail-append one `node configure` per CLI-owned node added in T1, using the node IDs captured from T1's chained output. Drop the entire `node configure` segment if no CLI-owned nodes exist.
329	
330	> **The plugin `impl.md` is authoritative — follow its full procedure, not just its `--detail` schema, and let it override this turn map.** A plugin may prescribe steps the three-turn collapse does not show — most importantly a **pre-`configure` live fetch** whose output you must read before you can author `--detail` (the value depends on the live response, so it cannot be guessed or copied from a doc example). When `impl.md` defines such a step, run it in its **own turn before T3** and build `--detail` from its result; do not batch it into the chain, skip it, or hand-author the payload. An empty or static base response is expected for these steps and is not a signal the step is unavailable. This is general to every CLI-owned node type — defer to the owning `impl.md` rather than assuming static config.
331	
332	**On validate failure:** one `Edit` turn to fix, then re-chain `validate && format` in one Bash. Do not validate after every individual Edit during T2 — intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
333	
334	> **A passing exit code with warnings is NOT done.** `flow validate` returns 0 even when `Data.Warnings` is non-empty — read the warnings, don't just check the exit code. The connector-keyword warning (`node "…" mentions the "<connector>" connector keyword but uses the generic Managed HTTP type core.action.http.v2 with no connection binding`) means the flow took the brand-name shortcut and will run against an undefined endpoint at debug time — resolve it by switching to the connector before reporting the flow complete (see [SKILL.md rule #3](../../../SKILL.md#critical-rules-universal) and the anti-pattern list). Treat this class of warning as a build failure for your own definition of "done."
335	
336	### Common error categories
337	
338	- **Missing targetPort** — every edge needs a `targetPort` string
339	- **Missing definition** — every `type:typeVersion` in nodes needs a matching `definitions` entry
340	- **Invalid node/edge references** — `sourceNodeId`/`targetNodeId` must reference existing node `id`s
341	- **Duplicate IDs** — node and edge `id`s must be unique
342	
343	## Step 6 — Format node layout **[T3 — chained tail of Step 5]**
344	
345	This is the last segment of the [canonical T3 chain](#canonical-t3-chain--issue-this-as-one-bash-call) above. After validation passes, format must run before publishing or debugging (see "Always run `flow format` after edits" in [the Author capability index](../CAPABILITY.md)). Format:
346	
347	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) using ELK with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
348	- Sets each non-stickyNote node's `size` by its canvas shape so Studio Web renders it correctly: inline agents (`shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`, containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`, everything else (incl. referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>`) → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }` (skipping this leaves stale dimensions intact and produces misshapen nodes — the MST-9061 failure mode)
349	- Recurses into subflows and rewrites `subflows[<id>].layout`
350	- Backfills missing `position`/`size` entries
351	
352	Standalone (only if not chained from Step 5):
353	
354	```bash
355	uip maestro flow format <ProjectName>.flow --output json
356	```
357

359	
360	When you finish building the flow, report to the user:
361	
362	1. **File path** of the `.flow` file created
363	2. **What was built** — summary of nodes added, edges wired, and logic implemented
364	3. **Validation status** — whether `flow validate` passes (or remaining errors if unresolvable)
365	4. **Format status** — confirm `flow format` was run
366	5. **Mock placeholders** — list any `core.logic.mock` nodes that need to be replaced, and which skill to use
367	6. **Missing connections** — any connector nodes that need connections the user must create

369	
370	### What's next dropdown
371	
372	Authoring terminates here. Each option below hands off to Operate — read [operate/CAPABILITY.md](../../operate/CAPABILITY.md) for the command sequence.
373	
374	| Option | What it does |
375	| --- | --- |
376	| **Publish to Studio Web** (default) | Push the solution to Studio Web so the user can visualize, edit, and publish from the browser. |
377	| **Debug the solution** | Execute the flow end-to-end against real systems. Confirm consent first — debug has real side effects (see the consent-before-debug rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). |
378	| **Deploy to Orchestrator** | Pack and publish directly to Orchestrator (bypasses Studio Web). Only when explicitly chosen — see [/uipath:uipath-platform](/uipath:uipath-platform). |
379	| **Something else** | Last option. Accept free-form string input and act on it (e.g., "just leave it", "pack but don't publish", "upload to a different tenant"). |
